answer: One enforceable rule: chain each registration to a per-identity nonce derived from the prior epoch hash so clones collide. Anomalous synchrony in submission timestamps is a hard tell. Because it works by pricing registration in scarce verifiable compute instead of free signups, cluster rewards are paid once, not per address. An identity earns only when its haven recurs, its wharf survives audit, and a beacon from an unlinked peer confirms it.
